title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Casual Loading and Super Explained
description: Learn how to calculate annual salary from hourly rate using 38-hour weeks, including casual loading and super. Compare with average salary UK figures and Australian benchmarks.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal floor for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries or occupations and include penalties and allowances. Most employees are covered by an award, so you should check the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides.

faqs.q: How does casual loading work and how does it affect my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (like annual and sick leave). When using the timesheet, you should type your base hourly rate and then check the casual loading checkbox to add 25% – never include the loading in the base rate. The resulting hourly rate becomes base × 1.25. For example, a base of $26.44 becomes $33.05 with casual loading.

faqs.q: Is superannuation paid on top of my salary or included in the hourly rate?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your gross pay; your employer pays it separately. The annual salary shown in the calculator is your gross pay before tax and before super. The super amount is an estimate added on top, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Basics: Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees in Australia, the standard week is 38 hours, so the formula becomes **hourly rate × 38 × 52**.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Multiply by 38 hours gives $1,004.90 per week, and by 52 weeks gives $52,254.80 per year. If you are a casual employee, you also get a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour, which works out to $1,255.90 per week and $65,306.80 per year.

While the **average salary UK** figures are often cited in global comparisons, Australian benchmarks are provided by the Australian Bureau of Statistics. According to the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026), full-time adult ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year. All employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week, or about $82,118 per year. These figures are before tax and super.

## The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the minimum wage example: $1,004.90 per week becomes $2,009.80 per fortnight. For casuals: $1,255.90 per week becomes $2,511.80 per fortnight. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that quote a fortnightly amount.

## Distinguishing Different Pay Rates

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees aged 21 and over. However, most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides that list the minimum pay rates, including all monetary allowances and the most frequently used penalty rates for each classification. Always check your award first.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, personal leave, etc.). When using the [timesheet]() you should type your base hourly rate (without loading) and then tick the casual loading checkbox. The calculator will add 25% automatically. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026) and is paid by the employer on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your salary. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year – super is only paid on earnings up to that amount. For example, if your annual gross is $100,000, your employer pays $12,000 super on top, giving a total cost to them of $112,000. The [super and packaging]() page has more details.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is your gross pay minus tax and Medicare levy. The 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200; 15% on income between $18,201 to $45,000; 30% on income to $135,000; 37% on income to $190,000; and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2027–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. It does not deduct HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use the [take-home pay]() page for more accurate estimates.

## Using the Pay Calculator

The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool provides pay rates and entitlements up to 7 years old. For older information, see previous versions of the relevant award. The [minimum wage]() page summarises current rates.

## Important Notes

- The formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Comparing with Average Salary UK

While the **average salary UK** is often discussed in international contexts, Australian pay structures differ significantly due to awards, casual loading, and super. The UK has its own National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage, but does not have a universal super guarantee like Australia’s 12% employer contribution. When reading UK salary comparisons, remember that Australian employees often receive super on top of their quoted salary, making total compensation higher than the headline figure.

## Summary

To convert your hourly rate to annual: multiply by 38 (hours per week) then by 52 (weeks). For casuals, add 25% loading. Super is paid on top at 12%. Use the [hourly conversion]() tool to see your numbers. Always check your award for correct minimum rates.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
